mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%) compresses the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.5% indicates a weak labor market, which typically precedes equity market rallies due to delayed Federal Reserve rate hikes, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 900) and a rise in consumer credit (RSAFS > 400000) signals sectoral stress in the housing market and increased leverage, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 900 AND RSAFS > 400000.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized rate > 2.5%) typically triggers Federal Reserve monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation rate > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of total non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, consistently generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically reduces corporate profit growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%) compresses the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.
